title: Variants of vision encoder
reading: The slide surveys the main training paradigms used to produce vision encoders, each anchored to a canonical paper: supervised learning (ViT, Dosovitskiy et al.), masked modeling (MAE, He et al.), auto-encoding (VQVAE, Van den Oord et al.), self-distillation (DINO, Caron et al.), and multimodal learning (CLIP, Radford et al.). A side element refers to the relative popularity of these different vision encoders when used inside multimodal LLMs.

visuals.description: An accompanying figure labelled 'Popularity of different vision encoders in Multimodal LLMs', presumably comparing usage frequency across the listed encoder families.
visuals.assertion: Vision encoder families are not equally adopted in multimodal LLMs; some (typically CLIP-style contrastive encoders) dominate usage.

concepts.name: VQVAE
concepts.why_it_matters: Auto-encoding approach producing discrete visual tokens.

concepts.name: DINO
concepts.why_it_matters: Self-distillation yields strong label-free visual features.

concepts.name: CLIP
concepts.why_it_matters: Multimodal contrastive training gives language-aligned visual features, the common choice for MLLMs.
